node_fixture.name: puppet_agent_standin
header: # MOCK-APPLY node fixture `puppet_agent_standin` (HQ 2026-10-27 ruling 7) for classes that declare
# `service { 'puppet': ensure => running, enable => true }` (node_base_domain_desktop). On the lab node a real agent
# daemon would start a catalog run of its own between the harness's run 1 and run 2, applying the catalog and hiding
# run-2 changes (gate v2 would no longer prove idempotency). The fixture adds a systemd drop-in that replaces
# puppet.service's ExecStart with a sleep, so Service['puppet'] is really enabled and started, but no agent runs.
# NOT verified with this fixture: the agent daemon itself running on its interval.
# Lifted by: a harness mode that tolerates a running agent daemon between runs 1 and 2 (HQ batch-7 ruling 2)
node_fixture.scope_evidence: puppet_agent_standin: file[/etc/systemd/system/puppet.service.d] is the drop-in directory; file[.../p8test-standin.conf] holds only [Service] ExecStart= reset and ExecStart=/bin/sleep infinity; exec[p8test puppet.service stand-in daemon-reload] is refreshonly systemctl daemon-reload before Service['puppet'] that loads it. All three serve the stand-in for the class's service { 'puppet': ensure => running, enable => true, provider => systemd } (node_base_desktop.pp line 107) and none changes a resource the class declares; within the stated scope
